title: Kenyan Boiled Maize
author: Mama Wanjiru

relatedDish.note: Boiled and roasted maize are the two great Kenyan maize street foods. Boiled maize (mahindi ya kuchemsha) is softer, more tender, and milkier — ideal for very fresh young maize. Roasted maize (mahindi ya kuchoma) has a smoky, charred character and firmer texture. Both are eaten with lemon and chilli salt.

desc: Mahindi ya Kuchemsha is the soft, tender counterpart to roasted maize — whole cobs boiled in salted water until the kernels are sweet, milky, and perfectly cooked. One of the simplest and most satisfying snacks in Kenya.
longDesc: Boiled maize is a staple of Kenyan street food stalls everywhere. Large pots of salted water bubble constantly, keeping freshly cooked cobs ready for the next customer. The boiling method preserves the natural milky sweetness of fresh young maize in a way that roasting cannot — the kernels stay plump, juicy, and tender. Served with lemon and salt, it is simple food at its very best.
steps: Husk the maize cobs and remove all the silk.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a rolling boil.
Add the maize cobs. Cover and boil for 25—35 minutes until the kernels are tender when pierced with a knife.
Remove from the water and allow to drain briefly.
Mix the serving salt and chilli powder together.
Dip the cut lemon into the salt mixture and rub generously over the hot cob.
chefTips: Use the freshest, youngest maize available — the milkier the kernels the sweeter the result.
Do not overcook — overcooked maize becomes starchy and loses its sweetness.
Adding a pinch of sugar to the boiling water enhances the natural sweetness.
commonMistakes: Overcooking — 35 minutes maximum for most maize.
Using old, overripe maize — starchy and tough.
reheating: Microwave briefly with a damp paper towel.
healthBenefits: Good source of B vitamins and fibre.
culturalNote: Boiled maize is one of the most universal Kenyan street foods — sold from large steaming pots at roadsides, markets, and bus stops across every county.

faqs.q: Which is better — boiled or roasted?
faqs.a: Both are beloved. Boiled maize is softer and milkier; roasted maize has a smoky, charred character. Many Kenyans have a strong preference for one or the other.

cookingScience: Boiling maize in salted water gelatinises the starch granules in the kernels, making them soft and tender. Salt in the water seasons the kernels throughout rather than just on the surface.
sustainabilityTips: Save the maize cooking water — it is nutrient-rich and can be used in soups or stews.
